_comment: Contracts for @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory, covering all 9 tools.
Drafted with derive_contract() from the server's own schemas and completed
by a human.
This server is a knowledge graph keyed by entity NAME, which makes it the
natural test of reference binding against real software: the agent reads
names out of the graph and passes them straight back to delete_entities.
A name pulled from a directory looks identical whether the principal chose
it or an injection did.
What a human supplied, because the deriver could not:
- every effect. delete_* are DELETE and IRREVERSIBLE; the graph has no
undo. create_* and add_observations are WRITE but not irreversible,
because they add rather than replace.
- `collection` on every parameter carrying an entity name.
derive_contract drafts collections from <noun>_id names only, and this
server calls them entityNames, names, relations and deletions -- so it
drafted nothing and reference binding would never have fired. That is
the per-API cost this project prices rather than denies.
- `payload_paths` on every parameter that mixes the two. `entities` is
[{name, entityType, observations}]: the NAME decides which record a
write lands on, the OBSERVATIONS are the note being written. Marking
the whole parameter authority denies every legitimate call, because a
summary the model composed is attributable to nobody; marking it
payload attributes nothing, which idensec.lint reported as
no-authority-parameter on a writing tool -- and was right to.
- `query` downgraded to payload: a search string on a read-only tool is
not a choice of what to act on.

contracts.description: Removes entities and every relation touching them.
